title: Count Items Below Zero
statement:
A packaging company stores `n` items, and you are given an array `temp` where `temp[i]` is the storage temperature (in degrees) required by item `i`.

Count how many items must be stored **below 0 degrees**, that is, how many values in `temp` are strictly less than `0`. An item that needs exactly `0` degrees does not count.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` space-separated integers `temp[0] ... temp[n-1]`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the number of items whose required temperature is strictly below 0.

examples.explanation: Only `-3` and `-1` are below zero. The `0` is not counted.
No temperature is negative, so no item needs sub-zero storage.
Every item requires a temperature below zero.

hints: You only need to look at each temperature once.
Keep a counter and increase it whenever the current value is strictly less than 0.
Be careful with the boundary: a temperature of exactly 0 is not below zero.
